The ruling is entirely practical-halakhic: when judgments (דינין) overpower a person, naming them in prayer makes them identifiable to the accusing forces (מקטרגים), allowing the judgments to intensify. The proof-cases (Noah's birth, Moses praying for Miriam) demonstrate this rule in narrative terms. A gematria remez is categorically different from a bechina: it is a concealment technique, not an assertion that two concepts share the same essential nature. The teaching does not employ the bechina relational structure at all. Package formation requires bechina edges; with zero such edges, no packages exist for Torah #174.
